metric_rationale:
The design deliberately contains conflict pairs (1-6) in which the first discriminating cue in validity order favors one option while the feature-wise tally favors the other. Restricting to exactly those trials where the two heuristics make opposite, well-defined predictions, the metric reports the proportion of choices consistent with the top discriminating cue (Take The Best).

Under TTB this proportion is (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta) + eps/2, i.e. near 0.85-1.0 for most parameter draws; under Tallying it is the complement, 1 - [(1-eps)*sigmoid(m*beta) + eps/2], i.e. near 0.0-0.15, since the tally margins on these pairs (3, 1, 2) all point the other way. The expected mean gap is roughly 0.75, while the per-subject spread comes only from lapse/temperature draws and binomial noise over ~36 conflict trials per subject, so between-subject variance should be small (on the order of 0.005-0.01). This makes the contrast large in mean and tight per subject.

I deliberately exclude the tally-tie trials (pairs 7-10), where Tallying is at chance rather than opposite, because including them would pull Tallying's value toward 0.5 and shrink the gap. I also exclude control trials where the heuristics agree, since they carry no discriminative information. The metric is well defined on a single subject's slice and on the pooled frame alike.

This is a within-subject DIFFERENCE score that cancels the nuisance parameters (beta, epsilon) for the competing theory while remaining maximally large for mine.

Two trial sets are extracted purely from the stimuli:
(1) AGREEMENT set: trials where the top discriminating cue and the tally point to the same option, with a large tally margin (|margin| >= 3) -- pairs 3/4 (4 vs 1) and 5/6 (5 vs 0).
(2) CONFLICT set: trials where the first discriminating cue points one way and the tally the other, with |margin| >= 2 -- pairs 9/10 (1 vs 4), 11/12 (1 vs 5), and 13/14 (TTB must descend to expert 3 while the tally is 3 vs 1 the other way).

The metric is P(choose the TTB-favoured option | agreement) - P(choose the TTB-favoured option | conflict).

Under Take The Best, the choice probability for the first-discriminating-cue option is exactly (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta) + eps/2 in BOTH sets, independent of tally margin, so the difference is ~0 for every parameter setting; per-subject deviations come only from binomial sampling over 24 + 36 trials (sd ~0.08), so it is tight around zero regardless of how beta and epsilon are drawn.

Under Tallying, the same quantity is (1-eps)*sigmoid(k*beta)+eps/2 in the agreement set and its complement in the conflict set, giving a difference approaching (1-eps) -- typically 0.6-1.0 and never negative.

Thus the two theories are separated by a large mean gap with modest, mostly lapse-driven between-subject variance, and the contrast is not trivially true for Tallying: if humans stop at the first valid cue the score sits at zero.

Contrast score: (rate of choosing the option favoured by the highest-validity discriminating expert on POLARITY-REVERSAL pairs) minus (the same rate on AGREEMENT pairs). Reversal pairs are those where the top-cue winner also carries the larger validity-weighted mass of 1s ([11111]v[00000], [11100]v[00011], [10000]v[00000], [10000]v[00010] and mirrors); agreement pairs are the classic conflict items ([10000]v[01111], [10000]v[01100] and mirrors) where the top-cue winner carries the smaller mass of 1s. Under TTB only the sign on the first discriminating cue matters, so the hit rate is the SAME quantity ((1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2) on both sets for every subject regardless of beta and epsilon: the difference is identically 0 up to binomial sampling noise (48 vs 24 trials -> per-subject SD ~0.09). Under PWEA a '1' is a negative flag, so on the reversal set the top-cue option is REJECTED (margins of 5.0, ~3.6, ~1.9, ~1.35 mean-weight units times k=beta*|s|>=0.7 make this near-deterministic), while on the agreement set PWEA mimics TTB and the same option is chosen. The difference therefore lands near -(1-eps)*0.9, i.e. roughly -0.4 to -0.8, with epsilon-driven dispersion only. Because the metric is a within-subject difference of two rates that share the same noise parameters, it cancels the lapse/temperature heterogeneity that otherwise inflates between-subject variance, giving a large mean gap (~0.55-0.6) with tight per-subject variance.

Within-subject contrast between two base pairs that TTB must treat identically but PWEA must treat oppositely.

Define 'hit' = choosing the option favoured by the Take-The-Best cascade (the option with the 1 on the highest-validity discriminating cue). The metric is hit-rate on the CONFLICT pair {[1,0,0,0,0] vs [0,1,1,1,1]} minus hit-rate on the DOMINANCE pair {[1,0,0,0,0] vs [0,0,0,0,0]}. Both base pairs appear in both A/B orders, 12 trials each per subject, so side bias cancels.

TTB: cue 1 discriminates on BOTH pairs, so the predicted choice probability for the TTB winner is exactly (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 on both. The difference is identically 0 for every beta and epsilon, i.e. the metric is pinned at 0 with only binomial noise (var ~0.02-0.03), independent of subject parameters.

PWEA (polarity s<0, compensatory weights): on the dominance pair the weighted mass of 1s is 2.0 (gamma=1) or 1.1 (gamma=0.1) for A and 0 for B, so PWEA REJECTS A -> hit rate well below 0.5. On the conflict pair the mass is 2.0 for A vs 3.0 for B (gamma=1) or 1.1 vs 3.9 (gamma=0.1), so PWEA ACCEPTS A -> hit rate well above 0.5, agreeing with TTB. Hence the difference is strongly positive (~0.5-0.9) for essentially the whole admissible parameter box, and crucially beta, |s| and epsilon largely cancel within subject, keeping between-subject variance modest.

So the expected values are ~0 (TTB) vs ~0.6-0.7 (PWEA) with small per-subject spread: a large, tight contrast that is not trivially true of PWEA (it is a signed, direction-reversing prediction about two specific stimulus structures that any one-reason rule cannot produce).

The decisive dissociation in this design is Class 3, the count-vs-weight reversal pairs 11/12 ([1,1,0,0,0] vs [0,0,1,1,1]). Both theories agree that a '1' is a warning flag, so no polarity confound is possible; they simply disagree about WHAT is counted. FC-LEX counts flags validity-blind and must therefore choose the two-flag option [1,1,0,0,0] at its single flat plateau accuracy h = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2, which for the admissible ranges (beta 1.3-2.7, eps 0.05-0.25) lies tightly around 0.78-0.85 with very little between-subject spread (parameter-induced sd ~0.04 plus binomial noise over the 12 trials of that pair). PWEA, by contrast, integrates validity-weighted mass: with the deliberately skewed validities the mass of [1,1,0,0,0] is 3.89 versus 1.11 for [0,0,1,1,1] at gamma=1, and the ordering already reverses at gamma ~ 0.25, so for the large majority of the admissible gamma range PWEA must REJECT the fewer-flag option, pushing this proportion down toward the lapse floor (~0.16-0.30). Integrating over gamma in [0.1,1.15] gives an expected value near 0.27, i.e. roughly a 0.55 gap from FC-LEX's ~0.81, with per-subject variance dominated by binomial noise plus a modest gamma-driven component. The metric selects these trials generically (counts differ, but the fewer-flag option carries the larger mean-1-normalised weighted mass, with a large weighted margin) rather than by hard-coded row indices, and falls back to all count/weight-conflict trials if the strong-margin set is empty, so it is well defined on both the pooled frame and any single subject's 12-trial slice.

Both critical pairs are EQUAL-flag-count pairs in which the single highest-validity expert (v=0.90) discriminates and is owned by the same side within each pair. Define x = 1 if the subject picks the option carrying the top expert's '1'.

Pair P1 = {[1,0,0,0,1] vs [0,1,1,0,0]}: the top-cue owner also carries the SMALLEST validity-weighted mass of flags (w1+w5 < w2+w3 for every admissible gamma), so PWEA (negative polarity, weighted integration) picks it -> x high.
Pair P2 = {[1,0,0,0,0] vs [0,0,0,0,1]}: the top-cue owner now carries the LARGEST weighted mass (w1 >> w5), so PWEA rejects it -> x low.

Hence PWEA predicts a large positive value of mean(x|P1) - mean(x|P2) (roughly 0.4-0.9 depending on gamma and beta*|s|).

FC-LEX cannot express this at all: on both pairs the counts are tied, so the lexicographic fallback fires with the SAME top discriminating expert owned by the SAME (top-cue) option, yielding p(x) = tie_bias identically on P1 and P2. Its expected metric value is exactly 0 for every parameter setting. Crucially, taking the difference cancels the subject-level tie_bias entirely, so FC-LEX's between-subject variance reduces to pure binomial noise over 12+12 trials, keeping the competing theory's distribution tight around zero. Mirror (A/B swapped) presentations are pooled automatically because x is defined by cue ownership rather than by screen side, so any side bias cancels.

The design's core disagreement is magnitude invariance. I restrict scoring to the two 'hard' constant-difference-of-one pairs where the base count is large (2-vs-3 in trials 5/6 and 3-vs-4 in trials 7/8), and I explicitly exclude the triage pair (2 high-validity flags vs 3 low-validity flags) by requiring that the sign of the count difference survives dropping the two least-valid experts. This leaves 24 clean trials per subject.

FC-LEX (advocated) is mathematically forced to its single flat plateau accuracy h = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 on these trials, exactly as on 0-vs-1: with beta in [1.3,2.7] and eps in [0.05,0.25] this lands around 0.78-0.85 with small per-subject spread (binomial sd over 24 trials ~0.08).

WC-ST predicts ratio-scaled evidence s = 0.267 (2v3) and 0.196 (3v4), which through its accelerating Weibull (theta in [0.34,0.46], kappa in [4.5,7.5]) gives cores of ~0.51-0.64, and its much larger lapse range (eps up to 0.48) compresses this further toward chance: roughly 0.50-0.58. Excluding the triage pair removes the bimodal reversal subgroup, so WC-ST's per-subject variance also stays tight (it is pinned near the chance floor).

Expected contrast: ~0.81 (FC-LEX) vs ~0.53 (WC-ST), a ~0.28 gap with per-subject sd ~0.10 on both sides, easily significant at N=25. It is not trivially true for my theory: if humans show the ratio-driven collapse, this metric will read near chance and falsify FC-LEX.

This is a within-subject Weber-ratio contrast that both theories can be scored on with identical trial-direction coding (choose the option with fewer flags), so it cannot be trivially true for my theory.

EASY group = count pairs with high ratio-scaled evidence s = (c_hi-c_lo)/sqrt(c_hi^2+c_lo^2+1): 0v1 (s=.71), 1v2 (s=.41), 2v4 (s=.44), 3v6 (s=.44). HARD group = count pairs with low ratio evidence but comparable or identical raw differences: 2v3 (s=.27) and 3v4 (s=.20, same raw difference of 1 as 0v1 and 1v2). I exclude the 2v3 pair whose surplus flags sit on the two droppable low-validity experts (trials 13/14) so that discrete triage subjects do not add bimodal dispersion to the hard group; likewise the equal-count tie pairs are automatically excluded (ca==cb skipped).

FC-LEX is sign-only and magnitude-blind: every trial in both groups has a strictly unequal flag count, so its accuracy is the SAME constant h = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 on every trial in both groups, for any beta and eps. Its expected metric value is exactly 0, with only binomial sampling noise across 40 easy / 20 hard trials per subject (var ~0.011), and the beta/eps heterogeneity cancels within subject.

WC-ST has an accelerating Weibull over s with threshold theta in [.34,.46] and kappa in [4.5,7.5]: easy-group core accuracy runs ~0.72-1.00 (mid ~0.91) while hard-group core is pinned near chance (~0.50-0.64, mid ~0.52). After lapses the expected gap is roughly 0.25-0.30, and the gap is positively driven by the same subject-level theta so it stays comfortably above zero for essentially every subject.

Expected: ~0.27 for WC-ST vs ~0.00 for FC-LEX, with per-subject variance ~0.02 and ~0.01, giving Welch t ~7 at N=25. Any flat plateau (FC-LEX) or a linear/Gaussian margin rule (which would push 2v4 and 3v6 up but keep 3v4 ~ 1v2) is distinguished from the pure ratio signature.
